name: Heterogeneous Azeotropic Separation Pyridine Water Toluene
description: A pyridine-water mixture, which forms a homogeneous azeotrope, is fed into a two-column heterogeneous azeotropic distillation system with toluene added as an entrainer. The entrainer exploits a heterogeneous toluene-water azeotrope to drive liquid-liquid phase splitting in a decanter, allowing the organic and aqueous layers to be routed separately. High-purity pyridine is recovered as the bottoms of the first column, while high-purity water is recovered as the bottoms of the second column, and the toluene-rich overhead is recycled back to the first column.
prompt: Separate pyridine and water from their azeotropic mixture using toluene as an entrainer in a heterogeneous azeotropic distillation process. The toluene entrainer exploits a liquid-liquid phase split to break the azeotrope, recovering high-purity pyridine and high-purity water as separate products with toluene recycled.

name: Hydrodealkylation Toluene to Benzene SRK Recycle
description: Toluene and hydrogen feeds are mixed and heated to reaction temperature before entering a conversion reactor where toluene is dealkylated to produce benzene and methane. The hot reactor effluent is cooled and passed to a vapour-liquid separator, where the hydrogen- and methane-rich vapour is recycled back to the reactor feed while the liquid fraction is reheated and sent to a distillation column. The distillation column recovers high-purity benzene as distillate while toluene-rich bottoms are pumped and recycled to the reactor feed mixer.
prompt: Simulate the hydrodealkylation (HDA) of toluene to benzene using a hydrogen feed at high temperature. The reactor effluent contains benzene, unreacted toluene, hydrogen, methane, and biphenyl byproduct; after cooling and separation, the hydrogen and methane-rich vapour and the unconverted toluene liquid are both recycled to the reactor feed.
notes: Ground-truth reference: VAL_03_reference.json. Source DWSIM file: Hydroalkylation_of_Toluene_to_Benzene.dwxmz. name: Natural Gas Dehydration TEG Absorption Regeneration
description: Wet natural gas containing water, acid gases, and light hydrocarbons is contacted with lean triethylene glycol in an absorber column where TEG selectively absorbs water from the gas stream, producing dry sales gas overhead and a water-rich TEG bottoms. The rich TEG is flashed, heated, and fed to a regenerator column where water and light hydrocarbons are stripped overhead as sour gas while high-purity lean TEG is recovered as bottoms. The regenerated TEG is cooled and pumped back to absorber pressure before being recycled to the top of the absorber.
prompt: Dehydrate a high-pressure natural gas stream containing methane, ethane, propane, isobutane, n-butane, isopentane, n-pentane, nitrogen, hydrogen sulfide, carbon dioxide, and water using triethylene glycol (TEG) absorption. The wet gas contacts lean TEG in an absorber to produce dry sales gas; the water-rich TEG is regenerated by heating and stripping, and the lean TEG is cooled, repressurised, and recycled to the absorber.
notes: Ground-truth reference: VAL_06_reference.json. Source DWSIM file: Drying_of_Natural_Gas_using_TEG.dwxmz. Property package not stated — Peng-Robinson inferred as standard for natural gas + glycol dehydration at high pressure. name: Extractive Distillation Acetonitrile Isopropanol Water Ethylene Glycol
description: A ternary feed of acetonitrile, isopropanol and water, which forms multiple binary and ternary azeotropes, is separated using a two-stage extractive distillation system with ethylene glycol as the entrainer. The first column recovers high-purity acetonitrile as distillate at sub-atmospheric pressure, while the second column recovers isopropanol-rich distillate at atmospheric pressure. The combined bottoms from both extractive columns are sent to an entrainer recovery column where water leaves overhead and high-purity ethylene glycol is recovered as bottoms and recycled.
prompt: Separate a ternary feed of acetonitrile, isopropanol, and water — a system with multiple binary azeotropes — using a two-stage extractive distillation process with ethylene glycol as the solvent. Recover high-purity acetonitrile and high-purity isopropanol as separate overhead products, with water removed and the ethylene glycol solvent recovered and recycled.

name: Syngas Production RLNG Steam Reforming Ammonia Plant
description: Re-gasified liquefied natural gas and steam are fed to a primary reformer where methane is converted to syngas via steam reforming reactions, followed by a secondary reformer where air injection provides nitrogen and additional combustion heat. The syngas then passes through high-temperature and low-temperature shift converters to maximise hydrogen yield by converting carbon monoxide, followed by a carbon dioxide absorber to remove CO2, and finally a methanator to eliminate trace carbon oxides, yielding a purified hydrogen and nitrogen rich syngas suitable for ammonia synthesis.
prompt: Produce a hydrogen and nitrogen-rich syngas for ammonia synthesis from regasified LNG (methane) and steam. Primary steam reforming converts methane to hydrogen and carbon monoxide; secondary reforming with an air feed introduces nitrogen and drives further conversion; high and low temperature shift reactors then convert carbon monoxide to additional hydrogen; carbon dioxide is absorbed and removed, and trace carbon oxides are eliminated by methanation.
